'''Subir Sarkar''' (12 September 1953, [[Ichapore]], India) is an Indian astroparticle physicist and cosmologist, known for his research on the [[Hidden sector|dark sector]] and astroparticle physics. He has been at the Rudolf Peierls Centre for Theoretical Physics, [[Oxford University]], since 1990, and was Head of the Oxford Particle Theory Group (2011-2019). He was also Niels Bohr Professor<ref>{{cite web|title=Niels Bohr Professorships|website=Danish National Research Foundation|url=https://dg.dk/en/niels-bohr-professorship/}}</ref> at the [[Niels Bohr Institute]], University of Copenhagen (2013-2018). Since 2021, he has been Emeritus Professor and Emeritus Fellow of [[Linacre College]], Oxford.

He was on the Advisory Board of the [[Gruber Cosmology Prize]] from 2014 to 2020<ref>{{cite web|title=Subir Sarkar|website=The Gruber Foundation Foundation|url=https://gruber.yale.edu/person/subir-sarkar}}</ref> and has served since 2021 on Commission C4 (Astroparticle Physics) of the
[[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics]].<ref>{{cite web|title=IUPAP C4 Members 2025-2027|website=The International Union of Pure and Applied Physics|date=10 January 2025 |url=https://iupap.org/who-we-are/internal-organization/commissions/c4-astroparticle-physics/c4-members/}}</ref>

==Education and career==
After completing secondary school in 1969, Sarkar studied at [[IIT Kharagpur]], where he graduated with a B.Sc. in 1972 and an M.Sc. in 1974. He then joined the [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]] (TIFR), where he was appointed as a research associate in the Cosmic Rays Group in 1979 and was awarded a PhD in Physics in 1982. In 1983, he was a visiting fellow at the [[International School for Advanced Studies]] (''Scuola Internazionale Superiore di Studi Avanzati''; SISSA) in [[Trieste]] and during 1984–1985 a research associate in [[CERN]]'s Theory Division. For the academic year 1985–1986, he was a visiting fellow at the [[University of Oxford]]'s Department of Astrophysics and during 1987–1988  a research associate in the [[Particle physics|HEP]] Theory Group of [[Rutherford Appleton Laboratory]] (RAL) in [[Chilton, Oxfordshire]].<ref name=CV>{{cite web|title=Curriculum Vitae: Subir Sarkar|website=Department of Physics, University of Oxford|url=http://www-thphys.physics.ox.ac.uk/people/SubirSarkar/SubirSarkar_CV.pdf}}</ref> From 1988 to 1989 he worked in [[Bhopal]] for an Indian [[NGO]] ([[Eklavya foundation|Eklavya]]), specialising in science education and popularisation.<ref name=briefCV>{{cite web|title=Title: Introduction to Cosmology (brief description of 5 lectures); Biography- Brief CV: Professor Subir Sarkar|website=indico.cern.ch|url=https://indico.cern.ch/event/432000/attachments/936841/1327383/sarkar.pdf}}</ref> In 1990 Sarkar became a staff member of the [[University of Oxford]]'s [[Rudolf Peierls Centre for Theoretical Physics]].  He was a visiting scholar at [[Wolfson College, Oxford]] from 1991 to 1993 and a research fellow from 1993 to 1997. During 1997-1998, he was a departmental lecturer and a tutor in physics at [[Pembroke College, Oxford]]. He was appointed as a University lecturer in 1998, promoted to reader in 2000, and professor in 2006, retiring as professor emeritus in 2021. Sarkar headed the Oxford Particle Theory Group from 2011 to 2019. He has also been an adjunct faculty member at TIFR and at the Raman Research Institute, Bangalore.<ref name=CV/>

Sarkar's research deals with relations between fundamental physics and aspects of astrophysics and cosmology<ref name=briefCV/> and has a wide range, including [[dark matter]], [[primordial nucleosynthesis]],<ref>{{cite book|editor-last1 = Klapdor-Kleingrothaus
|editor-first1 = Hans Volker 
|editor-last2 = Ramachers
|editor-first2 = Y  | chapter=Primordial nucleosynthesis and dark matter by Subir Sarkar  |last=Sarkar |first=Subir  | date=13 October 1997 | title= Dark Matter in Astro- and Particle Physics, Dark '96 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=MNFKDwAAQBAJ| publisher=World Scientific |pages=235–249|arxiv=astro-ph/9611232}}</ref> cosmological phase transitions, [[cosmological inflation]], large-scale structure of the universe,<ref name=briefCV/> and problems with the [[Lambda-CDM model|ΛCDM model]].<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://inference-review.com/assets/pdf/articles/heart-of-darkness.pdf|doi=10.37282/991819.22.21 | title=Heart of Darkness  |last=Sarkar |first=Subir  | date=2022 | journal=Inference: International Review of Science |issue = 6|page=4}}</ref> He has also participated in experiments such as the [[Pierre Auger Observatory]], the [[Big European Bubble Chamber]] (BEBC), the [[IceCube Neutrino Observatory]], and the [[Cherenkov Telescope Array]] in investigations of very high energy cosmic rays and neutrinos.<ref name=briefCV/> He is a member of the Dark Energy Science Collaboration of the [[Vera C. Rubin Observatory]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.physics.ox.ac.uk/our-people/sarkar |title=Prof Subir Sarkar|website=University of Oxford, Department of Physics }}</ref> He was a founder member of the India Oxford Initiative,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ox.ac.uk/news-and-events/find-an-expert/professor-subir-sarkar |title=Professor Subir Sarkar|website=News & Events, University of Oxford }}</ref> which began funding projects in 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=India Oxford Initiative|website=University of Oxford|url=https://www.india.ox.ac.uk/research}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Subir Sarkar is married to [[Amanda Cooper-Sarkar]], a particle physicist in the Department of Physics, Oxford University.

==Awards and honours==
In 2017, Sarkar was awarded the [[Homi Bhabha Medal and Prize]]. In 2021, he shared the [[Bruno Rossi Prize]] awarded to [[Francis Halzen]] and the IceCube collaboration.<ref name=CV/> Sarkar's collaborators and former students held a celebration from 11 to 13 September 2023 in honour of his career achievements and his 70th birthday.<ref>{{cite web|title=SubirFest|date=September 2023|website=University of Oxford|url=https://subirfest.web.ox.ac.uk/home}}</ref>
